about.title: Orinda Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Orinda residents rely on everyday products — from kitchen appliances to car components used along commuter routes like SR-24 — trusting they were built to be safe. When a manufacturing flaw, design defect, or missing warning label turns an ordinary object into a hazard, the resulting injuries can be sudden and serious. California law gives injured people a real advantage here: strict liability generally means you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that it caused your injury. That single distinction can make product cases different from other injury claims. If you were hurt by a defective item in Orinda, keeping the product exactly as it was at the time of injury matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can look at the facts of your situation and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Orinda Claims

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California strict liability rules, you generally only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each share liability for a defective product, which often gives injured Orinda residents more than one path to recovery.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Key Evidence
items.desc: Preserving the item exactly as it was at the time of injury can be critical, and an attorney can advise on how to protect that evidence early.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability doctrine typically requires showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company acted carelessly. This can simplify certain aspects of a claim compared to standard negligence cases.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product near SR-24 in Orinda — does that change anything?
items.answer: The location of the injury doesn't change the legal standard, but it can help establish a clear timeline and any witnesses nearby. What matters most is preserving the product and documenting how the injury happened.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without repairing, discarding, or altering it. This preservation can be important evidence, and an independent attorney can advise you on safe storage and next steps.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We are not a law firm and do not charge for the connection.
